# Which shard runs each UI test class.
#
# Every class in UITests/ is on exactly one line. CI's `plan` job fails when a
# class is on none or on two, or a line names a class that is gone, so a new
# test class means a new line here (and in `data-only.txt`, if it reads data).
#
# **Balanced on time, not on count.** The seconds are each class's median over
# five sharded runs of the whole suite on 29 October 2026, and are only used to
# balance: nothing fails if they drift. Sharded times, not the single
# simulator's, because the classes do not slow evenly: on shards
# `LayoutBudget` took 675 to 865 seconds against a single-simulator median of
# 552, while the suite as a whole ran 13% over, so a map balanced on the
# single simulator left its shard 2 to 4 minutes behind the rest.
#
# **Two exceptions, which came after.** `WinterCostumesOnTheDay`'s 187 is its
# one run on a single simulator, in #106's CI on 29 October, and
# `BackToTheDayYouWereOn`'s 201 is its one run of seven tests on a local
# iPhone 17 simulator on 5 November, added to the lightest shard rather than
# rebalancing the map.
# On a shard either may run over. Replace each with its sharded median once
# there is one.
#
# **Two more, `KeyAtEverySize` and `AStartThatFails`,** came on 5 November:
# their 63 and 6 are one local run each, on an iPhone SE. Replace them with
# their sharded medians too.
#
# **And `SoundWithTheRingerOff`,** on 9 November: its 10 is one local run on an
# iPhone 17 simulator, added to the lightest shard. Replace it the same way.
#
# To rebalance, or to change the number of shards, update the seconds and
# print a new map:
#
#   python3 .github/ui-tests/plan.py balance 4
#
# It minimises the slowest shard, and half the slowest shard's data-only share,
# so a data-only run is split evenly too. Within a shard, classes run in
# XCTest's order, whatever their order here.
#
# shard  class                              seconds
